bullets.text: Risk-on: leaning into risky assets, 3rd night in a row, VIX calm at 14.2.
Your book holds 5 positions, heat comfortable at 1.2%.

regime.title: Regime
regime.note: The market's mood. The label is decided by three inputs — the VIX, its term structure, and high-yield spreads; the other seven are tracked and shown but do not move it.

macro-drivers.title: Macro drivers
macro-drivers.note: The regime's three deciding inputs with their recent history.

regime-timeline.title: Regime timeline
regime-timeline.note: How the market mood and the VIX fear gauge have moved across recent nightly snapshots. Each dot is one snapshot; higher = more fear; dot color = that night's regime verdict (green risk-on, red risk-off, amber mixed).

candidates.title: Research candidates
candidates.note: Businesses worth reading about, screened quality-first.

research-reopens.title: Research reopens
research-reopens.note: Names already researched in depth and set aside, each with the stated evidence that would reopen the question.

scorecard.title: Ticker scorecard
scorecard.note: Stocks doing something statistically odd right now — dislocation, not quality.

about.heading: What this is
about.body: Every signal here is market microstructure — short interest, days-to-cover, oversold RSI, FTD spikes, retail chatter. A high score means something unusual is happening to the stock, usually a small one, and says nothing about the business.

about.heading: How much to trust it
about.body: Treat it as a to-research feed: most flags deserve rejection, and by design the research step kills nearly everything.

cot-tails.title: COT positioning tails
cot-tails.note: Futures markets where the professional crowd is all-in on one side of its own 3-year range.

about.heading: What this is
about.body: Weekly CFTC managed-money positioning, each futures market measured against its own 3-year range. A row appears only when a market sits in the bottom or top 15% of that range with at least a year of report history behind it.

about.heading: Why per-market
about.body: The composite's class-average positioning signal cannot see one market's extreme inside a mixed class: the week sugar sat at the 12th percentile of its range, the softs class averaged 33 and scored nothing.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: A washed-out short is a coiled spring — any bullish surprise forces funds to buy back at once; a crowded long is the mirror. Neither is a direction call on its own: it marks where a squeeze has fuel, not when it fires.

cot-tails.caveat: A tail marks a market to watch, not a trade: identical washouts have resolved violently or sat unchanged for months. No measured forward-return evidence yet.
cot-tails.empty: no futures market sits in the tail of its own 3-year managed-money range tonight

signal-recommendations.title: Signal recommendations
signal-recommendations.note: The verdict on each signal, graded against the base rate.
signal-recommendations.caveat: A backtest replay against ALFRED vintages, not live trading — read excess/beats-baseline, never hit-rate alone.
signal-recommendations.empty: insufficient evidence for every signal (young scorer) — expected; fills in once a signal's evidence crosses the reliability floor

signal-efficacy.title: Signal efficacy
signal-efficacy.note: Every signal's raw report card: how often it has been right so far.
signal-efficacy.caveat: Nominal and uncorrected across ~48 comparisons — hold every verdict loosely.
signal-efficacy.empty: no matured signal outcomes yet — appears once a signal's flagged calls reach their grading horizon

bucket-performance.title: Bucket performance
bucket-performance.note: Grouping every past opinion by conviction bucket: did stronger scores actually produce better forward returns than SPY?
bucket-performance.caveat: Several signals are graded at once, so a few clear the bar by luck.
bucket-performance.empty: no matured buckets yet — appears once conviction-bucketed opinions reach their grading horizon

equity-curve.title: Portfolio vs SPY
equity-curve.note: Your account's time-weighted growth of $100 against SPY's and overnight cash's.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: All lines start at $100 on the first charted date. Deposits and withdrawals are marked but excluded from the portfolio line — it moves only when the book's value moves, so a gap between the lines is skill (or its absence), never a transfer.

about.heading: The cash line
about.body: Daily fed funds (FRED's DFF) compounded over the same window — roughly what a T-bill fund or HYSA would have paid. SPY asks whether the picks beat the index; cash asks whether the money should be in the market at all.

human-filter.title: Human-filter tally
human-filter.note: Of the opinions this page flagged, you either acted or passed.
human-filter.caveat: Compares acted-on vs. passed-on flags from a still-small decision journal. A handful of trades can swing the comparison either way.
human-filter.empty: no matured flagged opinions yet — appears once an acted-on or passed-on flag reaches its grading horizon

regime-performance.title: Regime edge
regime-performance.note: Does the market-mood call itself have forward edge?
regime-performance.caveat: Regime windows are contiguous stretches, not independent draws.
regime-performance.empty: no matured regime outcomes yet — appears once a market-mood window reaches its grading horizon

book-heat.title: Advisor book heat
book-heat.note: How much of your account is genuinely at risk right now.

group-heat.title: Advisor group heat
group-heat.note: Correlated positions collapsed into single bets.
group-heat.empty: no group heat yet — appears once the advisor computes tonight's book

position-heat.title: Per-position heat
position-heat.note: Risk contribution of each individual holding.

disagreements.title: Disagreements
disagreements.note: Tickers where tonight's score points the opposite way from a position you already hold.

size-caps.title: Size caps
size-caps.note: A volatility-scaled ceiling on how large each candidate position could be.

trader-scorecard.title: Trader scorecard
trader-scorecard.note: A plain-text report grading past decision quality.
text_lines: Filter edge (acted vs passed, by horizon)
trader-scorecard.caveat: Grades the human's own decisions from the journal. Coverage is whatever got journaled, not a random sample of every flag shown.

candidate-efficacy.title: Candidates screen edge
candidate-efficacy.note: A name's first entry onto the candidates reading list starts a stopwatch.
candidate-efficacy.caveat: Episodes are few and overlap early. The view carries plain averages with no confidence interval, so read n before believing any row.
candidate-efficacy.empty: no matured episodes yet — first grades appear ~21 trading days after the first screen night

health.title: Pipeline health
health.note: Launchd job exit codes, hung jobs, log FAILED/STALE counts, and stale or empty databases — everything the retired nightly ntfy push carried.

pending.title: In-flight opinions
pending.note: Opinions already recorded whose outcome has not matured yet.
pending.caveat: These flags haven't reached their grading horizon yet, so nothing here is a result — it's a worklist.
pending.empty: nothing pending — everything registered so far has matured — fills once tonight's opinions are registered

basis-breaks.title: Data-integrity checks
basis-breaks.note: Days where a price moved so far that it looks like a split or a bad tick.
basis-breaks.empty: no basis breaks detected — an empty table is the good outcome; fills only when a price move looks like a split or a bad tick

research-filter.title: Research call grade
research-filter.note: When the research skill said buy or pass, how often was it right against SPY?

about.heading: How it is measured
about.body: Every research-ticker verdict starts a stopwatch. A buy is right when the name beats SPY over the horizon; a pass is right when it lags. Hit rate is the share of calls that were right.

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: This is the grade for the whole funnel's last step — the decision a human actually makes. Below 50% at n>30 means the research is adding noise, not signal.

research-filter.caveat: Hit rate is the safe headline; the excess column reads inversely on pass calls (a pass is right when the name lags), so compare it only within one call type.
research-filter.empty: no matured research verdicts yet; appears once a call's forward window closes

research-verdict-outcomes.title: Research calls, one by one
research-verdict-outcomes.note: Every graded research call with what the stock and SPY did afterward.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: One row per call and horizon. Excess is the stock's return minus SPY's; 'Right?' applies the call's own direction (a pass is right when excess is negative).

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: The grade above is an average; this is where you find the one call that dragged it, and whether the miss was a stock story or a market move.

flag-response.title: What you did with each flag
flag-response.note: Each composite flag, whether you acted or passed, and how the name moved afterward.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: 'acted' means a fill landed on the flagged name, 'passed' means you logged a deliberate no, 'inferred' means no record either way. Directional excess is the return in the flag's direction, minus SPY.

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: This is the row-level detail behind the 'Filter edge' tally: if the passes outperform the acted rows, your filter is subtracting value.

flag-response.empty: no matured flags yet; appears once a flagged name reaches its grading horizon

signal-effective-n.title: How much evidence, really
signal-effective-n.note: The signal report cards count rows; this counts independent episodes, which is the honest sample size.

about.heading: The problem
about.body: A signal that fires on ten consecutive days produces ten overlapping forward windows. They mostly share the same market weeks, so ten rows is closer to one observation.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: 'Distinct dates' collapses same-day rows; 'independent episodes' also merges runs of consecutive dates whose windows overlap. The sparkline is the hit rate on each flag date — a grade earned on one hot week shows as a single spike.

verdict.text: 1 of 1 signals rest on fewer than 3 independent episodes

signal-effective-n.caveat: A signal that fired on ten overlapping days is one observation, not ten. Trust the episode count over the row count.

candidate-outcomes.title: Candidates list, entry by entry
candidate-outcomes.note: What each name did against SPY after it first appeared on the candidates list.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: One row per list entry and horizon. 'Door' is which dislocation test let the name onto the list — an oversold RSI, a drawdown from the high, or both.

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: The screen's edge is an average over these rows. A single large winner can carry it, so scan the distribution before trusting the summary.

candidate-outcomes.empty: no matured list entries yet; appears 21 trading days after a name first enters the candidates list

candidate-quality-trend.title: Falling-knife check
candidate-quality-trend.note: For every name still on the candidates list, whether the business has weakened since it first appeared.

about.heading: What a falling knife is
about.body: A stock that looks cheaper every week because its price is falling faster than its earnings — the cash-flow yield rises while the F-score or return on capital drops. The level gates keep passing it; only the trend shows the problem.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: Each row compares the quality gates on the first sighting with the newest one. Flagged rows sort to the top; they are the names to re-research before buying more.

verdict.text: no falling knives on the list

candidate-quality-trend.empty: no candidate has been on the list for two sightings yet

option-pnl.title: Option premium P&L
option-pnl.note: Dollar profit on single-leg option trades, kept separate from the stock grades.

about.heading: How it is measured
about.body: Every option fill is a signed cash event in the premium ledger; a position's P&L is those events summed once it closes or expires. Premium return is P&L over the premium at risk.

about.heading: Why it is separate
about.body: Options are graded on dollars, stocks on return versus SPY — the two never mix, so a lucky expiry cannot flatter the stock-picking grade.

option-pnl.empty: no option fills journaled yet; appears with the first single-leg option fill synced into the journal

replay-efficacy.title: Backtest replay
replay-efficacy.note: Would the macro signals have worked in the past, using only the data that existed at the time?

about.heading: How it is measured
about.body: Each FRED series is replayed from its ALFRED vintages — the numbers as first published, before revisions — and each flag is graded on what SPY (or a sector ETF) did next. A report enters the replay only after its release date.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: Drift baseline is how often the benchmark simply rose over that horizon; excess is the flag's hit rate minus that. 'Beats drift' means the whole confidence interval sits above the baseline; 'anti-signal' means it sits entirely below — a signal reliably wrong is not a signal to flip.

replay-efficacy.caveat: Nominal and uncorrected across ~48 comparisons; a lone 'beats drift' at p≈0.04 is what chance produces. Read excess against the baseline, never hit rate alone — the benchmarks drift up, so a bullish flag 'wins' by doing nothing.
replay-efficacy.empty: no replay yet; runs Saturdays after the ALFRED vintage pull

replay-baseline.title: Benchmark drift
replay-baseline.note: How often each benchmark simply went up over each horizon — the bar every replayed flag has to clear.

about.heading: Why it exists
about.body: Stocks drift upward, so a bullish flag that does nothing still 'wins' most windows. Every replay grade is measured against this null, never against 50%.

replay-flags.title: Replay flags today
replay-flags.note: What each replayed signal is saying right now, with its score over the last 90 flag days.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: Score is the flag's vote: positive bullish, negative bearish, zero quiet. The sparkline shows how long it has held that view.

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: This is the live edge of the backtest — the same signal definitions the replay graded, applied to the newest vintage.

exit-advice.title: Exit suggestions
exit-advice.note: For each holding, where a stop would sit and whether the size has outgrown the signals behind it.

about.heading: How it is computed
about.body: The stop is the price after a one-ATR adverse day from here; 'room to stop' is how far away that is. A trim appears when the position is larger than the advisor's cap for its current score.

about.heading: What to do with it
about.body: Nothing automatic happens. Read a trim as 'the signals no longer support this size' and a tight stop as 'one bad day is close' — then decide.

exit-advice.caveat: Decision support only. A stop here is a suggested distance from a one-ATR adverse day, not an order anywhere.
exit-advice.empty: no positions in the latest snapshot

option-heat.title: Option legs
option-heat.note: Each option position's share-equivalent exposure and what a one-ATR move would cost.

about.heading: How it is computed
about.body: Delta × contracts × 100 is the share-equivalent; heat is that many shares moving one ATR. A protective put counts negative and offsets the shares it covers in the group view.

about.heading: Uncovered legs
about.body: A leg with no delta input or a short leg is marked uncovered — its risk is unknown or open-ended, so the book heat number above it is a floor, not a total.

option-heat.empty: no option legs held in the latest snapshot

order-queue.title: Order queue
order-queue.note: Buys you have queued that have not yet been placed.

about.heading: How it works
about.body: You queue a buy with a reference price and a maximum gap; the morning slot places it at the open only if the live quote is within that band, otherwise it vetoes and the row lands in the run results.

about.heading: Why it is on the page
about.body: A queued order is a pending commitment of real money — it should never be a surprise the next morning.

order-queue.empty: the queue is empty; nothing will be placed at the next open

order-runs.title: Execution runs
order-runs.note: Every queued order the executor has processed and what happened to it.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: 'placed' means an order went to the broker under the limit ceiling; a veto names the gate that stopped it (price gap, cap, market closed). Outcome is the broker's final state where known.

order-reconciliation.title: Unreconciled orders
order-reconciliation.note: Orders the executor placed that the journal has not yet seen a fill for.

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: The journal is what the grades run on. A placed order with no fill row means either the broker never filled it or the nightly journal sync missed it — both need a look.

verdict.text: every placed order has a journal fill

order-reconciliation.empty: every placed order has been matched to a journal fill

week-ahead.title: This week
week-ahead.note: Every scheduled release and earnings report this week, plus the Fed and expiry dates that shape it.

about.heading: What is in it
about.body: Economic releases from the official calendar, confirmed earnings dates, the next FOMC meeting and whether the Fed is in its pre-meeting quiet period, the next monthly options expiry, and the next early market close.

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: A high-impact release or an FOMC day is the most common reason a signal moves for reasons that have nothing to do with the stock.

yield-curve.title: Treasury yield curve
yield-curve.note: Short and long Treasury yields and whether the curve is inverted, straight from the Treasury's daily table.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: Normally the 10-year pays more than the 2-year. When it pays less the curve is 'inverted' — historically a recession warning, though the timing is loose.

federal-debt.title: Federal debt and the Treasury's cash
federal-debt.note: Total public debt and the government's checking-account balance over the last 90 days.

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: When the Treasury rebuilds its cash balance it drains reserves from the banking system; when it spends it down it adds them. Either way it is liquidity moving in the background of every price.

federal-debt.empty: no debt or TGA rows yet

funding-markets.title: Funding markets
funding-markets.note: Overnight rates and the Fed's balance sheet — the plumbing that shows stress before prices do.

about.heading: What the numbers are
about.body: SOFR is the overnight rate banks actually borrow at; IORB is what the Fed pays on reserves. SOFR trading above IORB means cash is scarce. SOMA is the Fed's bond portfolio; reverse repo is cash parked at the Fed overnight.

fred-series.title: FRED series
fred-series.note: Every tracked economic series with its year-over-year change and how unusual today's level is.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: Z-score is how many standard deviations the latest value sits from the series' own history — beyond ±2 is rare. The tiles are the regime's raw inputs; the regime card above turns them into a verdict.

verdict.text: 0 series more than 2σ from their own history

cot-positioning.title: Futures positioning — legacy report
cot-positioning.note: Where large speculators sit in each futures contract, and which contracts are at a positioning extreme.

about.heading: What the COT index is
about.body: Speculators' net position, scaled 0–100 against its own three-year range: 100 means the most long they have been, 0 the most short. Extremes tend to precede reversals because there is nobody left to join the trade.

about.heading: The three reports
about.body: The CFTC publishes the same data three ways: this legacy split (commercial vs speculator), a disaggregated split for commodities, and a financial-futures split. The other two have their own cards.

cot-positioning.empty: no legacy COT report loaded yet

cot-disaggregated.title: Futures positioning — commodities
cot-disaggregated.note: Managed money versus the producers and merchants who actually handle each commodity.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: Managed money is hedge funds; commercials are producers and processors hedging real supply. When the two indexes sit at opposite ends the commercials have usually been right.

cot-disaggregated.empty: no disaggregated COT report loaded yet

cot-financial.title: Futures positioning — financials
cot-financial.note: Leveraged funds versus dealers in equity-index, rate and currency futures.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: Leveraged funds are the fast money; dealers are the banks on the other side of their trades. A leveraged-fund index near 0 or 100 marks a crowded position.

cot-financial.empty: no financial-futures COT report loaded yet

auction-demand.title: Treasury auction demand
auction-demand.note: How eagerly the last thirty Treasury auctions were bid, against each security's usual demand.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: Bid-to-cover is dollars bid per dollar sold; below its typical level means buyers wanted a higher yield to show up. A run of weak auctions pushes long rates up.

upcoming-auctions.title: Upcoming Treasury auctions
upcoming-auctions.note: Announced auctions in the coming weeks — supply days that can move rates.

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: A large coupon auction on the same day as a data release is the classic set-up for a rates surprise.

upcoming-auctions.empty: no auctions announced in the window

dark-pools.title: Dark pools
dark-pools.note: How much trading happened off the public exchanges last week, and on which venues.

about.heading: What a dark pool is
about.body: A private venue where large orders trade without showing on the public order book. FINRA publishes each venue's weekly volume with a two-week delay.

dark-pools.empty: no ATS weekly file loaded yet

off-exchange-leaders.title: Most-traded off exchange
off-exchange-leaders.note: The symbols with the most dark-pool volume last week, with their weekly trend.

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: Institutions work large orders in the dark. A symbol whose off-exchange share is climbing is being accumulated or distributed by someone big — the direction is not shown.

off-exchange-leaders.empty: no ATS weekly file loaded yet

sec-revisions.title: Restated financials
sec-revisions.note: The newest cases where a company's later filing changed a number it had already reported.

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: A restatement is a company correcting its own past. Small ones are routine; a large one on revenue or net income is a reason to read the filing.

sec-screener.title: Largest filers
sec-screener.note: The biggest companies by reported revenue, straight from their XBRL filings.

about.heading: Where it comes from
about.body: The SEC's company-facts feed — the audited numbers themselves, not a data vendor's copy. The candidates screen reads the same feed for its quality gates.

sec-screener.empty: no XBRL company facts loaded yet

ftd-spikes.title: Fails-to-deliver spikes
ftd-spikes.note: Securities whose delivery failures jumped far above their own normal on the latest settlement date.

about.heading: What a fail is
about.body: A trade where the seller did not deliver the shares on time. A spike often means shares are hard to borrow — a crowded short.

ftd-spikes.empty: no fails-to-deliver spikes on the latest settlement date

ftd-largest.title: Largest fails by dollar value
ftd-largest.note: The biggest delivery failures on the latest settlement date, in dollars.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: Dollar value is fails × price. Large-cap names appear here on routine settlement noise; a small-cap here is the interesting case.

ftd-streaks.title: Persistent fails
ftd-streaks.note: Securities that have failed to deliver for the most consecutive days and are still failing.

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: A fail that persists past the regulatory close-out window means someone is being forced to buy in — a mechanical source of demand.

short-volume-ratio.title: Heaviest short selling today
short-volume-ratio.note: Symbols where an unusually large share of today's volume was short sales.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: FINRA reports each day's short volume per symbol. A high ratio can mean bearish conviction — or market makers hedging heavy call buying. The sparkline shows whether it is new.

short-volume-ratio.empty: no symbol above the short-ratio threshold today

short-volume-streaks.title: Sustained short pressure
short-volume-streaks.note: Symbols that have stayed above the short-ratio threshold for the most consecutive days.

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: One heavy day is noise; a streak is a campaign. These are the names where the short side has been leaning for weeks.

short-interest-crowded.title: Most crowded shorts
short-interest-crowded.note: Symbols where it would take the longest to buy back every short share at normal volume.

about.heading: What days-to-cover means
about.body: Shares short divided by average daily volume. Ten days means shorts need two weeks of the entire market's volume to exit — the fuel for a squeeze.

unusual-options.title: Unusual option activity
unusual-options.note: Option contracts that traded far more today than exist in open interest.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: Volume ÷ open interest above 1 means more contracts changed hands today than were outstanding — new positioning, not old positions closing. Whether it is a bet or a hedge is not visible.

unusual-options.empty: no unusual option contracts on the latest snapshot

options-sentiment.title: Options-market mood
options-sentiment.note: The fear gauge, the put/call ratios and the VIX term structure — the regime's raw Cboe inputs.

about.heading: What the numbers are
about.body: The VIX is the market's expected 30-day swing; above 25 is fear, below 20 calm. Put/call above 1 means more hedging than betting. VIX above VIX3M ('backwardation') means the next month scares people more than the quarter.

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: These three are the regime card's voters, shown here raw so you can see how close the call was.

dealer-positioning.title: Primary dealer positions
dealer-positioning.note: What the Fed's primary dealers hold, from the NY Fed's weekly survey.

about.heading: Status
about.body: The current fetch returns no rows for this domain; the card stays so the gap is visible rather than silent.

dealer-positioning.empty: the NY Fed primary-dealer feed returns no rows for this query — empty by design until the fetcher's series filter is revisited

earnings-confirmed.title: Confirmed earnings dates
earnings-confirmed.note: Upcoming earnings reports whose dates the company has confirmed, not estimated.

about.heading: Why confirmed matters
about.body: Estimated dates slip. A confirmed date is when the options market's implied move becomes a real deadline for any thesis on the name.

earnings-confirmed.empty: no confirmed earnings dates in the window

market-closures.title: Market holidays
market-closures.note: Upcoming NYSE closures and early closes — days the executor must not expect an open.

about.heading: Why it is under Ops
about.body: The order executor and every trading-day calculation key off this list. An early close ends the intraday window early.

energy-inventories.title: Energy inventories
energy-inventories.note: Weekly US crude, product and gas stocks with the change from last week and a year's trend.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: A draw (negative change) tightens supply and supports prices; a build does the opposite. The sparkline shows the seasonal pattern the weekly number sits inside.

ag-balance.title: Grain balance sheets
ag-balance.note: For each major crop, how much will be left over at the end of the marketing year relative to use.

about.heading: What stocks-to-use means
about.body: Ending stocks divided by total use — the cushion. A low ratio means any weather scare hits price hard; a high one means supply can absorb surprises.

wasde.title: WASDE world balance
wasde.note: The USDA's monthly world supply-and-demand estimates by commodity and region.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: The same stocks-to-use ratio as the card above, but from the monthly WASDE report and split by region — the number grain traders wait for each month.

reddit-trending.title: Reddit attention
reddit-trending.note: The tickers gaining the most mentions across stock subreddits in the last 24 hours.

about.heading: How to read it
about.body: Rank and mentions come from ApeWisdom's tally. Attention is a crowding measure: a name everyone is talking about has no one left to discover it.

reddit-trending.caveat: Crowd attention, not information. A mention spike tells you a name is crowded — which cuts both ways.

insider-activity.title: Insider filings
insider-activity.note: Companies with the most insider transaction filings in the retained window.

about.heading: What a Form 4 is
about.body: Officers and directors must report their own trades within two days. Filing count alone does not say buy or sell — click through to EDGAR for the direction.

insider-activity.empty: no insider filings in the retained window

recent-filings.title: Recent event filings
recent-filings.note: The newest 8-K and other event filings from tracked companies — something happened and had to be disclosed.

about.heading: What an 8-K is
about.body: A 'current report' a company must file within four days of a material event: an acquisition, a departure, a restatement, a covenant breach. The form code says which.

recent-filings.empty: no event filings in the retained window

offerings.title: Share offerings
offerings.note: The newest registration statements and prospectuses — companies preparing to sell stock.

about.heading: Why it matters
about.body: An offering adds supply and usually prices below market. A name on the candidates list that files one is about to dilute you.

offerings.empty: no offering filings in the retained window

stakes.title: Activist and large-holder stakes
stakes.note: New 13D and 13G filings — someone crossed the 5% ownership line.

about.heading: 13D vs 13G
about.body: A 13D is an active holder who may push for change; a 13G is passive. Either is a large buyer revealing itself.

stakes.empty: no 13D/13G stake filings in the retained window

glossary.VIX: The CBOE Volatility Index — the market's expected 30-day volatility, derived from S&P 500 option prices. Higher means more fear.
glossary.Regime: This page's one-word read on market mood — risk-on, risk-off, or mixed — decided by the VIX, its term structure, and high-yield credit spreads.
glossary.Coverage: The fraction of catalog signals that actually produced a reading for a given ticker tonight, out of every signal that could apply.
glossary.Piotroski score: A 0-9 score of balance-sheet and profitability quality; higher generally means a financially healthier company.
glossary.Heat: Quantity times ATR — the dollars at risk on a one-ATR adverse day for a position, book, or correlated group of positions.
glossary.Score sum: The net vote across every independent signal that fired for a ticker tonight — positive leans bullish, negative leans bearish.
